provenance.basis: Reconstructed standing depiction of August Billings, helper in the Glessner household (inferred: the 1900 census enumerates him as a helper in the rear building behind the house, born January 1875 in Sweden, single; no source read says he was still there on 1 July 1904), standing in the stable yard at the alley end of the court, on the carriage drive just inside the courtyard gates and about a metre off the stable's south wall, facing east into the court. The gates, the drive and the coach house are the house's own (HABS sheets 2-3; Glessner's The Story of a House, 1923). A helper's work in a private stable (cleaning and harnessing the horses, the stable and the carriages) is read from Mrs. Seely's Cook Book (1902); his working dress, a striped shirt in shirt sleeves with braces and a belt, dark trousers and a light felt hat, is built after Frances Benjamin Johnston's groom of about 1902 (T-3484). Where he stands and when, his face, hair and complexion are reconstructed: no picture of him is known.
provenance.replaceable_by: A photograph of August Billings or of the Glessner stable staff, or a record that he was or was not working at 1800 Prairie in 1904; his place in the stable yard and his standing have no documentary claim.
